name: Tramadol
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Tramadol and its active metabolite (M1) build up as kidney function falls. For immediate-release (IR) tramadol, the most common form in the Philippines, the US label lengthens the dosing interval to every 12 hours with a maximum of 200 mg/day when creatinine clearance (CrCl) is below 30 mL/min. Extended-release (ER) tramadol should not be used at CrCl below 30 mL/min because its fixed strengths do not allow safe dose adjustment.

bands.recommendation: IR: 50 to 100 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed after titration, maximum 400 mg/day; over 75 years, maximum 300 mg/day (label). ER: usual dosing, maximum 300 mg/day (label).
IR: no adjustment at CrCl ≥30 (label). ER: no consistent change in tramadol exposure at CrCl 30–80; M1 exposure 20–40% higher (label). Use with caution.
bands.short: No change at CrCl ≥30; use with caution

bands.recommendation: IR: increase the dosing interval to every 12 hours, maximum 200 mg/day (label: CrCl <30). ER: do not use (label).
bands.short: IR q12h, max 200 mg/d; ER: avoid

hd.text: IR: dose as for CrCl <30 (every 12 hours, maximum 200 mg/day); give the regular dose on dialysis days, since less than 7% is removed in a 4-hour dialysis (label). ER: do not use.
hd.short: IR q12h, max 200 mg/d; ER: avoid

pd.text: IR: dose as for CrCl <30 (every 12 hours, maximum 200 mg/day); no PD data. ER: do not use.
pd.short: IR q12h, max 200 mg/d; no PD data

crrt.text: No data. ER: do not use; IR: specialist input.

dialyzable: No: less than 7% removed in a 4-hour dialysis (label).
monitoring: Respiratory depression, sedation, seizures, serotonin syndrome, hypoglycemia, hyponatremia; opioid boxed warnings.

pediatric.approved_ages: Not established in pediatric patients. Contraindicated under 12 years, and under 18 years after tonsillectomy and/or adenoidectomy (label).

renal.recommendation: Not established in children. Contraindicated under 12 years; 12 to 17 years: avoid with respiratory risk factors (label). Age, not kidney function, determines use.

pediatric.notes: Avoid in adolescents 12 to 18 years with risk factors for respiratory depression (obstructive sleep apnea, obesity, severe lung or neuromuscular disease) (label).
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)

adult: IMPORTANT: Fetcher chose an extended-release capsule label (Trigen, NDA022370). Most PH tramadol products are immediate-release (often with paracetamol). The IR (Ultram) label has CrCl <30 interval-extension dosing; it was NOT available, so IR rows say 'specialist input'. Fetch the IR label before approval.
Label text contains an apparent error: 'severe renal impairment (Child-Pugh Class C)'. Child-Pugh is a liver score. Do not reproduce.
pediatric: Contraindicated under 12 years per label; nothing extrapolated.
